browser: Chromium 156.0.8078.4, headless, via playwright-core 1.56.1 (local WSL2 Linux x64)
note: expected_http_error_console_lines are the browser's own log lines for intentionally provoked failures (revision conflicts, a rejected element, refused tokens after simulated and real API restarts, save failure, save conflict, connection resets that drop create responses, a refused token before an unconfirmed create is resent, two failed autosaves, a late autosave reply held until the page moved to a copy, an edit refused after another client moved the session, a refused token when an edit to a copy reaches a restarted service, read-only storage, a document busy behind a CLI's save lock, save replies the page never got, a copy whose first reply was dropped and whose check was answered request_in_progress, a move to the trash refused for unsaved changes, and a rename refused because the document changed elsewhere). The document-list steps search, sort, rename through the dialog, move a document to the trash after confirmation, restore it, refuse a rename whose document changed elsewhere (the list then shows it as it is, and Reload with no document open only reads the list again), and check the list at 320 px. The storage-feedback steps make documents/ read-only, hold a save lock in a CLI process (detected with a non-blocking flock probe), hold one save reply 11 s past the page's 10 s deadline, drop two save replies with a connection reset after the service answered, and answer a copy first with a dropped connection and then with request_in_progress; they check how many requests the page sent and that all carried one request ID. The steps that make documents/ or drafts/ read-only (read-only storage, the failed autosaves, and the left-open copy) are skipped when running as root, since permissions do not stop root, and are then listed in skipped_steps. edits_while_a_request_is_pending delays transactions by 400 ms. The recovery steps kill the API process with SIGKILL and start a new one. Before a kill that follows a draft discard or a copy, they wait for the page's list read that those trigger: CI run 40652695710 failed once when the kill cut that read off and the development proxy answered it 502 (a test synchronization race; the same sequence exists on main). Drawing a bond waits until the page has taken in the edit's reply: CI run 40654403437 on main failed once when the draft state still read "saved" for the revision before, so the left-open copy step made drafts/ read-only before the edit was drafted (the original's draft then lagged its document by one revision). 40-fold CPU throttling around that step reproduces the failure without the wait and passes with it. The list step makes its two documents an hour old before the rename: the recency order is the files' modification time, and WSL2's clock stepped back about 0.7 s between two writes in 2 of 8 local runs (see document-management.json). The simulated-restart step used to fail now and then (#8; 1 of 20 runs on main): a request started just as the step's one-time route was used stalled in the browser, because playwright-core 1.56.1 turns request interception off when the last page route goes away. The smoke now keeps interception on with a context-wide pass-through route, and the step waits for the retried edit's response; see browser-route-race.json. The placement step duplicates a drawing as a second scene instance, moves it with its arrow buttons, adds an atom that the page places in both instances, drags an atom in the second instance only, undoes that drag, and duplicates again, checking the graph and the first instance through the API after each step and that the third instance is copied from the last (moved) one, offset by (40, 80). The recorded-states step sets, in the inspector, three stated hydrogens and a doublet radical on a bonded carbon (drawn H3C, the hydrogens on the left because its bond leans right), attachment point 1 on the other bonded carbon, and an aromatic bond, and leaves an isolated nitrogen with inferred hydrogens (drawn as N with no count). It then places iodine and chlorine (a narrow and a wide symbol) and a query list N, O, S, P, Se with the Element buttons, and later gives the chlorine a charge (drawn Cl+) and the query two stated hydrogens (drawn ![N,O,S,…]H2). On the nitrogen it presses charge then query, and query then charge, and on the list it types a new list and presses the negation, each time with the first /transactions request held until the second action is in: no request is refused, the query atom carries no charge, and the list keeps both the typed elements and the negation. After the fonts have loaded it measures the rendered SVG in every placement: no element has textLength or lengthAdjust (glyphs are never stretched); each text chunk's getBBox lies inside the box the canvas computed for that chunk (its data-box), and each chunk box and radical dot inside the label's box; the text before and after a symbol (H3C, Cl+, and the query's H2, measured with getExtentOfChar) is drawn within 2 pt of it, not apart from it; no stroke of a bond ends inside a label's box; every label box, placement frame and placement ID lies inside the SVG view box; and no stroke collapses. It also checks the labels' and the bond's accessible names, which name the placement ("Atom a1 in s1: …") because the drawing has several. The same drawing is checked after save, after a page reload, and after closing and reopening from storage. editor-states.png shows the result; with this step, two runs in a row passed. This result: one local run with CHEMIFREE_SMOKE_NO_SKIPS=1, using the Chromium version above. It holds the group response while another object is selected and holds a move while Delete is queued; Undo must restore the selection at the Delete press. A separate intentional mutation that recorded the later selection failed this Undo assertion, and the source was restored byte for byte. The earlier runs cited above used other browser versions. Every run writes results.json, build.log, environment.json, requests.log, api.log (--log-requests), and web.log; a failed run also writes failure.png. CI runs it in the browser job; see browser-ci.json. This later run also deletes a selection changed immediately before the keypress, and deletes a reference owner together with its target before undoing the deletion. Both behaviors were reproduced as failures before their fixes. The P11 draft-preservation follow-up also passed the complete smoke locally with this browser and no skipped steps.
